A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RoboSense dataset and benchmarks. The main text, figures, Tables 1–9, and complete appendices support comparison despite the changed title, terminology, and pagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset statistics and experiments on detection, tracking, motion forecasting, and occupancy prediction, including sensor-layout and matching-criterion comparisons.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark outcomes in Tables 4–7 and the supplementary results and statistics in Tables 8–9.

M1.justification: The annotation pipeline, ICP-assisted occupancy generation, CCDP matching criterion, late-fusion procedure, and BEVDepth occupancy adaptation remain unchanged in Sections 3–5 and Appendix B. The robot-oriented terminology does not establish a procedural or architectural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same RoboSense collection from 22 locations and the same six benchmark tasks. Table 2 retains all scene statistics. Changes such as S5 becoming 'sidewalks' and S6 becoming 'streets' rename retained coverage; no navigation evaluation is added.

E2.justification: Tables 4 and 9 retain the same four LiDAR and four image detection methods. AB3DMOT, ViP3D, PnPNet, the constant/random-motion comparisons, and the BEVDepth occupancy baseline also remain in their corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: The splits, sensor configurations, input resolution, voxel sizes, matching thresholds, prediction horizon, and occupancy evaluation procedures are retained. Section 4.1.1 shortens the mAOS/mASE discussion to AOS/ASE, consistent with the per-class metrics already reported in v1; no changed evaluation procedure is specified.

E4.justification: The sensor-layout/range study, matching-function comparison, annotation-distribution plots, ICP illustration, and scene examples are retained. Exchanging examples between Figure 1 and Figure A6 adds no case study. Table 1 adds descriptive counts without introducing a new ablation or robustness test.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the benchmark scores. Both retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds annotation counts within 5 m, including RoboSense's 173K, KITTI's 638, and nuScenes' 9.8K, and changes Waymo's listed duration from 5.5 to 6.4 hours. Benchmark scores in Tables 4–7 and 9 remain identical. v4 also removes v1's BEVDepth improvement figures of 2.0% and 2.2%, which did not match Table 4.

T1.justification: The CCDP rule, underlying metric calculations, and Appendix A coordinate transformations remain unchanged. v4 omits the standard class-average mAOS equation and accompanying mASE averaging explanation, but introduces no different mathematical argument, assumption, or formal property.

C1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion redefine the central contribution from a dataset for outdoor low-speed autonomous driving to one for egocentric perception supporting autonomous agents in crowded, unstructured environments. The claimed 'first dataset' novelty is correspondingly broadened beyond functional vehicles.

C2.justification: Section 5.6.1 adds a specific explanation linking persistent near-field failures to obstacles occupying large portions of the view, causing truncation and occlusion. Conversely, the related-work discussion drops v1's explicit statement about the absence of lane-boundary and traffic-sign signals.

D1.justification: v4 adds a first-page 'Code & Dataset' repository link, providing an explicit access pointer absent from v1. Sensor specifications, synchronization, implementation settings, and supplementary annotation procedures are otherwise retained. The PDFs alone do not establish the linked resource's availability.

R1.justification: The same 42 bibliography entries remain, but the relationship to prior datasets is substantially reframed. v1 emphasizes filling the high-speed versus low-speed driving gap; v4 positions RoboSense as addressing a distinct egocentric social-robot navigation domain beyond existing automotive benchmarks.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, positioning paragraphs, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around egocentric robotics. Results discussion gains explicit topic labels, metric exposition is shortened, scene terminology is standardized, and author/header information changes. This exceeds routine copyediting.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains year and near-field-count columns and reordered rows. Figures 2 and 3 exchange positions, examples are exchanged between Figure 1 and Figure A6, and the sensor illustration is revised. Tables 6–7 become vertically stacked; most other displays retain their structure and content.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves usability and clarity through the explicit resource link, concrete near-field counts in Table 1, and clearer organization of results. Removing the inaccurate BEVDepth improvement figures also improves consistency. These gains are limited: benchmark evidence is unchanged, and the broader robot-navigation positioning receives no additional empirical validation.
